heading: What did you need to do?

the-answer.title: The answer
the-answer.script: In this party example, three useful capabilities might help address the gaps. This is a synthesis, not a universal checklist for every person or team.

break-down.title: Break down
break-down.script: First, work back from the goal. In this example, that helps assign someone to plan the ride home and tell guests what to wear.

write-contracts.title: Write contracts
write-contracts.script: Second, clarify important handoffs: what a task receives and delivers, and how its result can be checked. Here, defining the dietary requirement would help avoid the egg-dish mismatch.

review-twice.title: Review twice
review-twice.script: Third, check results against both the agreed task and the broader goal. In this example, that could flag an activity some guests cannot join.

the-organisation.title: The organisation
the-organisation.script: The organisation also shapes the conditions: clear goals, useful handoffs, task-specific oversight choices and workflows designed around the goal rather than the org chart.

look-at-your-team.title: Look at your team
look-at-your-team.script: Now look at your team. Where would it help to strengthen planning, clear handoffs or checking an agent's result? Those are useful capabilities to develop, based on this example and the evidence in the Speaker notes.

take-one-process.title: Take one process
take-one-process.script: And before Monday, do the smallest version of all of this. Pick one recurring process in your team, mark which steps an agent could run, and decide for each whether a person stays in, on or out of the loop.
